title: Cutting a Machine Call
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a finite state set, and let $M$ be a $k$-tape Boolean machine with states in $S$. Suppose that for every parameter $a$ there is a time $t$ no greater than a prescribed natural-number budget, with $t>0$, such that the run from state $\mathrm{en}$ and tape words $\mathrm{before}(a)$ does not visit state $\mathrm{ex}$ at any positive time strictly before $t$, and at time $t$ reaches state $\mathrm{ex}$ with tape words $\mathrm{after}(a)$. Then there exist a finite state set and a $k$-tape Boolean machine, together with start and finish states, such that for every $a$ some time within the same budget reaches the finish state with tape words $\mathrm{after}(a)$ from the start state and words $\mathrm{before}(a)$, and the finish state is not visited at any earlier time.
hypotheses_covered: A finite state set $S$ with decidable equality
Before and after tape-word assignments indexed by $A$
For each parameter, a time within budget, positive, with no visit to $\mathrm{ex}$ at positive earlier times and with the specified final configuration
